nodes.title: SG-2.5 · Mocked-dependency unit tests for the manifest loader
nodes.body:
Context: game/src/assets/loaders/manifestLoader.ts exports loadManifestFile, loadManifestWithFallback and checkAssetRefs. Existing tests (tests/manifestLoader.test.ts, manifestFallback.test.ts) use real temp directories, and tests/manifestRefs.test.ts covers checkAssetRefs in memory. Desired behavior: a suite where node:fs is fully mocked covers valid and invalid manifests, dangling references and missing-asset fallbacks. Why: the sub-goal requires all dependencies mocked.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given node:fs is mocked, when loadManifestFile and loadManifestWithFallback run, then no real disk access occurs
- Given valid, schema-invalid, unreadable and missing-asset inputs, when the loader runs, then each yields the asserted result
- Given refs absent from the manifest, when checkAssetRefs runs, then each dangling ref is reported


## Scope
- In scope: New mocked unit tests for the manifest loader
- Out of scope: Changing loader behavior
- Out of scope: Browser or e2e checks
- Preserve: Existing manifest tests
- Preserve: Loader public API


## Technical constraints
- vitest with vi.mock('node:fs')
- Tests live in game/tests


## Definition of done
- New mocked test files exist in the working tree and pass


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Loader valid, invalid and missing-asset fallback paths are proven with fs mocked
nodes.body:
With readFileSync and existsSync mocked, loadManifestFile and loadManifestWithFallback must be shown to return ok for a valid manifest, parse errors for a schema-invalid manifest, a 'cannot read manifest' error for an unreadable or malformed file, and a filtered manifest plus missing list when asset files are absent.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a valid manifest and existsSync true, then loadManifestFile returns ok true
- Given a schema-invalid manifest, then loadManifestFile returns ok false and the fallback returns an empty manifest with errors
- Given existsSync false for one asset, then the fallback lists it in missing and keeps the others


## Scope
- In scope: loadManifestFile
- In scope: loadManifestWithFallback
- Out of scope: checkAssetRefs
- Preserve: Existing behavior


## Technical constraints
- No real filesystem access


## Definition of done
- All paths asserted with mocked fs


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Dangling asset references are reported against a loader-produced manifest with fs mocked
nodes.body:
After a manifest is loaded through mocked fs where one file is missing, refs to the dropped asset and to unknown ids must be reported by checkAssetRefs as dangling while present ids pass.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a loaded manifest missing asset 'b', then checkAssetRefs(['a','b','ghost']) returns issues for 'b' and 'ghost' only
- Given all refs present, then it returns an empty array


## Scope
- In scope: checkAssetRefs combined with loadManifestWithFallback
- Out of scope: Loader changes
- Preserve: checkAssetRefs signature


## Technical constraints
- No real filesystem access


## Definition of done
- Dangling-reference scenarios asserted


## Clarifying questions
- None

acceptance_criteria: Invalid and unreadable manifests produce errors and an empty fallback

steps.action: Add vi.mock('node:fs', () => ({ readFileSync: vi.fn(), existsSync: vi.fn() })); tests: valid manifest JSON string with existsSync true gives ok true; JSON with a zero dimension gives ok false with path naming the dimension; readFileSync throwing gives error path 'manifest'; existsSync false gives error 'missing asset file'

Add tests: existsSync false for one of two assets gives missing length 1 and manifest.assets length 1; schema-invalid JSON gives empty manifest, errors non-empty and fallbackAssetId equal to FALLBACK_ASSET_ID; readFileSync throwing gives empty manifest and one error; call vi.resetAllMocks in beforeEach
steps.expected: Fallback tests pass and no real file is read
